brief.purpose: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions by proving Swing Shack's TrackMan technology gives golfers data-driven insight their game has been missing.
brief.audience: Jozi golfers, 25-50, mid-high handicap. They track their fitness — they want to track their golf. Data-aware, skeptical of voodoo tips, willing to pay for evidence-based improvement.
brief.bigIdea: Your swing has a number. TrackMan measures it. That number is the shortcut to better scores.
brief.successMetric: Fitting sessions booked. Secondary: GMB posts live weekly. Tertiary: engagement rate on stat-hook content above 2.5%.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A hook that stops the scroll with a specific number. A visual that shows TrackMan data overlaid on a club or swing. A caption that earns the click by expanding the data story. Booking link front and centre.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Vague transformation claims ('From confused golfer to confident striker'). Busy backgrounds without contrast. Price-led content without data justification. Anything that looks like generic golf marketing.

dna.tone: Clinical authority. Data speaks, we just translate it. No hype, no fluff — numbers are the argument. Authoritative but not cold. Expert without being gatekeeping.
dna.contentMix: 70% educational (data insights, stats explainers) / 20% promotional (session offers, fitting deals) / 10% social proof (client results, before/after)
forbiddenVisualStyles: text over busy backgrounds without contrast layer
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Direct price-led with anchoring: show the value first (TrackMan data), then introduce the offer. Always include R-amount. 'From R250' works because the data has already justified the price.

platformStrategy.instagram: Stat-first hook stops the scroll. Data overlay on image tells the story. Caption expands with context. Link in bio drives booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the number/stat itself. 'Your drive: 199m' as text overlay. 3-second hook, then explain the data. Fast-cut, punchy.
platformStrategy.gmb: Trust + proof + convenience. Service highlight with one key stat. Clean, professional, no gimmicks. Call to action is always 'book now' or 'call us'.

pillars.name: The Absurdity Mirror — showing the obviously wrong
pillars.description: Owns the 'hook' — presenting the cognitive dissonance that makes golfers pause and reconsider. This pillar delivers the uncomfortable comparison that sparks self-recognition. All initial awareness content lives here. Goal: create the 'wait, that's me?' moment.

pillars.name: The Cost of Mismatch — quantifying the damage
pillars.description: Owns the 'pain point education' — explicitly connecting wrong clubs to specific performance problems: inconsistency, lost distance, slicing, fatigue. Uses data and relatable examples. Goal: make the problem feel real and costly enough to act upon.

pillars.name: The Fitting Reveal — demystifying the solution
pillars.description: Owns the 'process clarity' — showing exactly what a club fitting involves, who performs it, what technology is used, and how long it takes. Removes barriers to booking. Goal: transform fitting from intimidating mystery into accessible opportunity.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — proving it works
pillars.description: Owns the 'social proof and credibility' — real Johannesburg golfers showing real results after fitting: lower handicaps, more consistent ball striking, regained confidence. Goal: make booking feel safe and inevitable.

pillars.name: The Right Now Urgency — time to act
pillars.description: Owns the 'conversion pressure' — limited-time offers, seasonal reasons to fit NOW (start of golf season, pre-summer tournament prep), and scarcity messaging around fitting slots. Goal: convert awareness into immediate action.

dna.tone: Confrontationally helpful — wakes golfers up with an uncomfortable truth, then delivers them to relief. Sharp enough to create pause, warm enough to invite action. Like a trusted friend who tells you the unflattering truth.
dna.contentMix: 30% Provocative Problem Education / 25% Transformation Proof / 20% Fitting Process Clarity / 15% Urgency Micro-Moments / 10% Community Social Proof
requiredContentTypes: golfers in action with proper clubs
preferredVisualStyles: dramatic low-key lighting with warm spotlights
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like the natural, relieving next step after discomfort — not a hard sell. 'Book Your Fit' carries weight because we've just shown them why they need it. One clear action, no ambiguity.

platformStrategy.instagram: Use carousel format for the split-comparison reveal (swipe to see the 'wrong tool' slide then the golf equivalent). Reels for quick educational hooks. Stories for behind-the-scenes fitting moments. Highlight tab for testimonials.
platformStrategy.gmb: Lead with the 'wrong clubs' problem in the description. Pin a post showing the absurdity comparison. Use Google Posts to share fitting success stories with specific score improvements. Respond to reviews mentioning equipment changes.

visualDirection.mood: A warehouse gallery at midnight — dramatic spotlights cutting through darkness, revealing truth.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visual concept: A golfer stands in a void, half illuminated by harsh white spotlight, holding a driver that looks comically wrong — perhaps a pool noodle taped to a tennis racket. The other side of the frame shows the same golfer in warm golden light, holding proper fitted clubs. The contrast should feel almost theatrical, like a David Fincher scene where the hero confronts their limitation. Use deep shadows to create mystery, then reveal clarity. Every visual should ask 'are YOU using the right tools?' without being preachy. Show the BEFORE state as darker, more chaotic, the AFTER as golden and composed.
imageReferences: a split image: left side shows someone attempting to dig with a pool noodle in harsh shadow, right side shows a golfer gripping an obviously wrong club in low light with frustrated body language
a backlit silhouette of a golfer mid-swing with the club head blurred to create tension, overlaid with text 'Your clubs don't match your swing'
a fitter's hands holding a launch monitor readout next to a club lying on a fitting mat, golden hour warmth contrasting with dark workshop background

visualDirection.colorUsage: The warm orange (#FF6B35) functions as the alarm — it's the uncomfortable truth, the moment of confrontation. Use it sparingly but powerfully: a slash across the 'wrong' side of comparisons, or as urgent text callouts. The gold (#D4AF37) is the solution — it appears when proper equipment enters the frame, creating positive reinforcement. The near-black background (#0D0D0F) isn't just aesthetic; it creates the 'stage' effect where the truth gets revealed. White text ensures readability against this darkness. The palette mirrors the campaign's emotional arc: discomfort leads to clarity.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serifs for headlines — something like Bebas Neue or Oswald. The contrast between thick, almost aggressive headlines and clean body text creates the same tension as the visuals. Use ALL CAPS sparingly for maximum-impact phrases. The typography should feel like a documentary title card — authoritative but not corporate.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split compositions are mandatory for comparison posts — 50/50 or 60/40 divisions with stark contrast between sides. Left (problem): dark, harsh lighting, orange accents. Right (solution): warm, golden, inviting. Leave negative space at the bottom third for text overlays. Use diagonal lines sparingly to create dynamic tension, not chaos.
contentExamples: Carousel: Slide 1 shows someone running a marathon in flip-flops. Slide 2 shows a golfer using 10-year-old hand-me-down clubs. Slide 3: 'Still making sense?' Slide 4: 'Book a fitting to make sure YOUR clubs match YOUR game.'

Reel concept: 6-second hook — golfer shanking a shot. Slow-mo. Text: 'Not your fault. Maybe your clubs.' 15 seconds: quick cuts of launch monitor data, fitter explaining, clubs being adjusted. End card: 'Book Your Fit.'

GMB post: Side-by-side image of 'wrong tool for the job' (spoon to dig a trench) vs 'wrong clubs for your swing' (generic driver vs fitted). Caption: 'We fixed equipment. We fixed consistency. We fixed scores.' CTA to book.

dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like the natural consequence of a revelation, not a sales push. After showing the problem, invite them to experience the solution with a complementary practice session or fitting consultation. Make it feel like the obvious next step after curiosity strikes.

platformStrategy.instagram: Carousels work perfectly for the comparison concept - build the paradox across slides and end with the golf revelation. Reels can show the split-screen wrong-tool scenarios in motion. Use strong hooks in the first 3 seconds. Instagram Stories for quick educational tips and Q&A engagement around equipment questions.

Use the Q&A feature to answer common equipment questions. Posts should feel educational and credible, building trust for when prospects are ready to book.

visualDirection.mood: Dramatic, revelatory, confident - a spotlight moment where truth meets opportunity
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should contrast wrong-tool absurdity with golf reality. Start with familiar wrong-equipment scenarios - running in dress shoes, cooking with a toy spatula - then pivot to the hidden wrong-club problem. Use dramatic lighting and high contrast to make the point hit harder. The visual journey moves from comedic recognition to serious consideration. Show real golfers mid-swing with clubs that don't match their game, then transition to properly fitted equipment in golden light representing the solution. Split-screen layouts work best - the left side shows the wrong-tool scenario in everyday life, the right side shows the equivalent wrong-club scenario on the course. Both should evoke the same visceral 'that's ridiculous' response.

visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background creates drama and forces the eye to focus on the contrast between wrong (orange warning) and right (gold solution). Orange signals urgency and alerts viewers to the problem they're experiencing. White text provides maximum contrast for readability against dark backgrounds. Gold appears only in the solution moments, making it feel earned and premium - the reward for recognizing the problem. This palette mirrors the campaign arc: alarm (orange) leading to resolution (gold).
visualDirection.typography: Bold, confident sans-serif headlines that land with impact. Use uppercase for key phrases to create emphasis and urgency. Body text should be clean and readable, supporting the headline without competing for attention. Numbers and data points should use a slightly different weight or color to stand out as evidence.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Visual contrast as the organizing principle. Before/after splits, side-by-side comparisons, and sequential reveals that build toward the solution. Leave breathing room - don't crowd the canvas. The dark background means elements float in space, creating drama. Use the gold accent sparingly but strategically to highlight the payoff moments.
